security_audit.summary: All static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md and adjudicated as false positives from Markdown examples. No executable code, prompt injection, environment access, reconnaissance, network behavior, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Realistic API key placeholder in documentation
remediation.suggestion: Replace sk_live_abc123 with YOUR_API_KEY or a clearly fake value, and avoid query-string key examples unless strongly discouraged.

remediation.issue: Unlabeled generic code fences trigger static scanner noise
remediation.suggestion: Use explicit fence languages such as http, json, yaml, or text for examples, so scanners can classify documentation correctly.

content.value_statement: Teams often create APIs with inconsistent routes, responses, and status codes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise REST patterns for predictable API design.
actual_capabilities: Defines REST resource naming rules using noun-based, plural URLs.
Maps HTTP methods to create, read, update, and delete behavior.
Recommends consistent response, error, and pagination structures.
Explains status code choices for success and error responses.
Covers filtering, sorting, field selection, versioning, and rate limiting.
Provides an API design checklist for endpoint reviews.
limitations: Focuses on REST APIs, not GraphQL, gRPC, or event-driven APIs.
Provides guidance only; it does not generate or validate OpenAPI files automatically.
Uses generic examples that need adaptation for each product domain.
Does not replace security, privacy, or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Standardize backend endpoints
use_cases.description: Review route names, HTTP methods, status codes, and response shapes before implementation.

use_cases.title: Align product API behavior
use_cases.description: Create shared rules for pagination, filtering, versioning, and error handling across teams.

use_cases.title: Improve developer documentation
use_cases.description: Turn endpoint decisions into clear request, response, and error documentation.
use_cases.target_user: Technical writers and developer relations teams

prompt_templates.title: Review a new endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one planned REST endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this REST endpoint proposal for naming, method choice, status codes, and response shape. Suggest simple improvements using the API design skill.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a resource model
prompt_templates.scenario: Design a small resource set before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design REST resources for this product area. Recommend resource names, relationships, nesting depth, and core operations.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize errors and pagination
prompt_templates.scenario: Create shared conventions for a growing API.
prompt_templates.prompt: Define consistent error responses, pagination, filtering, sorting, and field selection rules for our REST API.

prompt_templates.title: Design a versioned API surface
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for an API with long-term client support.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a versioning and compatibility strategy for this REST API. Include migration guidance, deprecation rules, and documentation requirements.

output_examples.input: Review a user management endpoint set before implementation.
output: Routes are grouped around user resources and related orders.
Create, read, update, and delete behavior uses the expected HTTP methods.
Validation, authentication, and not found cases receive distinct status code guidance.

output_examples.input: Create documentation requirements for a new public API.
output_examples.output: The response lists required endpoint descriptions, parameter details, request bodies, response schemas, examples, and error cases.

output_examples.input: Improve collection endpoints that return large result sets.
output: Pagination is required for every collection endpoint.
Filtering and sorting rules use predictable query parameters.
Rate limit headers are included so clients can adapt requests.

best_practices: Start with resource nouns and choose stable names before designing actions.
Document success and error responses for every endpoint.
Add pagination, filtering, and rate limits before collections grow.
anti_patterns: Use action verbs in URLs when a resource name is clearer.
Return success status codes for validation or authorization errors.
Expose internal database fields directly in public responses.

faq.question: What type of APIs does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on REST APIs with resource-based URLs, HTTP methods, JSON responses, and OpenAPI-style documentation.

faq.question: Can it generate a full OpenAPI specification?
faq.answer: It can guide structure and examples, but it does not automatically validate or generate complete OpenAPI files.

faq.question: Does it cover authentication design?
faq.answer: It includes basic bearer token and API key documentation patterns, plus reminders about safer authentication choices.

faq.question: Is this useful for existing APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to review routes, responses, pagination, status codes, and documentation for consistency gaps.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. It gives API design guidance, but separate security, privacy, and compliance reviews are still needed.
